title: This Fish's Fangs Are So Long Its Skull Has Holes for Them
subject: payara fish

scenes.text: This fish couldn't close its mouth if its skull didn't have holes.
It's the payara of the Amazon, and it has two long fangs on its lower jaw.
It's a fish hunter. It strikes other fish, even piranhas, and stabs them on those fangs.
But the fangs are so long they'd hit the roof of its mouth, so the upper jaw has sockets.
The fangs slide into the pockets, the mouth shuts, and the prey is trapped.
So the holes aren't a flaw. They're what lets it keep its dinner.

description:
The payara has fangs so long its skull has sockets to hold them.
Those pockets let it shut its mouth on fish, even piranhas.
Would you swim near this one?
first_comment: Fangs or venom: which would you rather face in the water?
